work_items: Active worker contention is not an implementation failure: When an autonomous IMPLEMENT request encounters a valid unexpired worker lease owned by another request, the conflict must escape candidate-admission…
validations: AC-01 Active worker contention is not an implementation failure: When an autonomous IMPLEMENT request encounters a valid unexpired worker lease owned by another request, the conflict must escape candidate-admission…

AC-02: validate protected requirement — The API returns HTTP 409 with fixed code `AUTONOMY_IN_PROGRESS` and bounded ordinary-language guidance. The response contains no worker owner ID, checkpoint payload, model/provider detail or raw exception text.

AC-03: validate protected requirement — The competing request must not change run state/revision/resume stage/failure code, worker state/revision/checkpoint/lease, source lineage, acceptance evidence or durable stage attempts.

AC-04: validate protected requirement — An expired worker lease continues to classify PROCESS_LOSS and may enter the existing STALLED → RECOVERING → REASSIGNED path only when current protected recovery policy admits it.

AC-05: validate protected requirement — Non-active lease conflicts that represent terminal, human-required, ready-for-integration or otherwise incompatible worker state remain governed by their existing protected rules and are not mislabeled as ordinary in-flight contention.

AC-06: validate protected requirement — Within one `useEngineeringRun` instance, synchronous duplicate continuation entry cannot issue a second autonomy request while the first continuation promise is active.

AC-07: validate protected requirement — A structured 409 `AUTONOMY_IN_PROGRESS` causes the client to read the latest canonical Engineering Run and keep it visible without publishing a Needs Attention failure. It does not invent progress or start another request in the same call.

AC-08: validate protected requirement — 409s without `AUTONOMY_IN_PROGRESS`, provider failures, validation failures and ordinary protected stage failures continue through existing error/recovery behavior.

AC-09: validate protected requirement — Automatic operation keys and expected Engineering Run revisions remain server-bound exactly as before. Single-flight handling grants no stage transition or replay authority.

AC-10: validate protected requirement — Automated tests model one request holding an active worker lease while a second request enters the same IMPLEMENT revision and prove the second request cannot mark the run failed while the first owner remains valid.
risks: AC-14 Regression proves the observed race cannot recur: Automated tests model one request holding an active worker lease

protected_acceptance_map.title: Active worker contention is not an implementation failure
protected_acceptance_map.protected_requirement: When an autonomous IMPLEMENT request encounters a valid unexpired worker lease owned by another request, the conflict must escape candidate-admission and implementation-failure classification. No `AUTONOMOUS_IMPLEMENT_FAILED` attempt may be persisted by the competing request.

protected_acceptance_map.title: Concurrency response is fixed and structured
protected_acceptance_map.protected_requirement: The API returns HTTP 409 with fixed code `AUTONOMY_IN_PROGRESS` and bounded ordinary-language guidance. The response contains no worker owner ID, checkpoint payload, model/provider detail or raw exception text.

protected_acceptance_map.title: Engineering Run and worker state remain unchanged by the loser
protected_acceptance_map.protected_requirement: The competing request must not change run state/revision/resume stage/failure code, worker state/revision/checkpoint/lease, source lineage, acceptance evidence or durable stage attempts.

protected_acceptance_map.title: Existing expired-lease recovery remains intact
protected_acceptance_map.protected_requirement: An expired worker lease continues to classify PROCESS_LOSS and may enter the existing STALLED → RECOVERING → REASSIGNED path only when current protected recovery policy admits it.

protected_acceptance_map.title: Terminal and protected worker states remain fail-closed
protected_acceptance_map.protected_requirement: Non-active lease conflicts that represent terminal, human-required, ready-for-integration or otherwise incompatible worker state remain governed by their existing protected rules and are not mislabeled as ordinary in-flight contention.

protected_acceptance_map.title: Same-hook client continuation is single-flight
protected_acceptance_map.protected_requirement: Within one `useEngineeringRun` instance, synchronous duplicate continuation entry cannot issue a second autonomy request while the first continuation promise is active.

protected_acceptance_map.title: Client treats AUTONOMY_IN_PROGRESS as read-only reconciliation
protected_acceptance_map.protected_requirement: A structured 409 `AUTONOMY_IN_PROGRESS` causes the client to read the latest canonical Engineering Run and keep it visible without publishing a Needs Attention failure. It does not invent progress or start another request in the same call.

protected_acceptance_map.title: Other API failures retain current handling
protected_acceptance_map.protected_requirement: 409s without `AUTONOMY_IN_PROGRESS`, provider failures, validation failures and ordinary protected stage failures continue through existing error/recovery behavior.

protected_acceptance_map.title: Operation/revision authority remains unchanged
protected_acceptance_map.protected_requirement: Automatic operation keys and expected Engineering Run revisions remain server-bound exactly as before. Single-flight handling grants no stage transition or replay authority.

protected_acceptance_map.title: Regression proves the observed race cannot recur
protected_acceptance_map.protected_requirement: Automated tests model one request holding an active worker lease while a second request enters the same IMPLEMENT revision and prove the second request cannot mark the run failed while the first owner remains valid.
